what: Willis Towers Watson is an insurance broker and advisory firm. It arranges insurance and reinsurance for companies, and advises employers on pensions, employee benefits and pay.
customers: Large and mid-sized companies buying insurance, insurers buying reinsurance, and employers managing pension and benefit schemes.
money: benefits consulting, pension advice and pay data
moat: Client relationships that renew annually and advisory work embedded in employers' pension and benefit administration, which is slow and risky to move.
risks: Revenue fell about 2% last year after business disposals
Commercial insurance rate softening reduces commission income
It has grown more slowly than Marsh and Aon for several years
opportunities: Operating margin of 23% after a long cost programme
Brokerage revenue does not require capital and converts well to cash
Pension and benefits advice is steady recurring work
watch: Organic revenue growth in Risk and Broking, and margin expansion.
